_comment: The graph-database contract: ONE answer key, four frameworks, four engines.
Feature 139.
A URL-selected graph data layer shaped EXACTLY like the relational Database
layer: GraphDatabase.create(url) picks an adapter by scheme, exposes one
portable node/edge/traverse surface PLUS a raw query()/execute() pass-through
in each engine's native language (Ultipa GQL/UQL, Neo4j/Memgraph Cypher,
ArangoDB AQL). Engine drivers are OPTIONAL and loaded only when used, so the
zero-dependency core is preserved. See
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/decisions/ADR-0059.md and
tina4-documentation/plan/v3/features/139-graph-databases.md.
PROVIDER MATRIX: every invariant below is a PER-ENGINE case. Each framework's
suite parameterises the same case names over every provisioned engine (Ultipa,
Neo4j, Memgraph, ArangoDB) - provider substitutability, exactly like the SQL
engine matrix. NO MOCKS: real connections, real round-trips against live
engines on the lab (Ultipa community edition is already up; Neo4j/Memgraph/
ArangoDB are provisioned via Docker behind the require-services gate, each with
its own TINA4_TEST_<ENGINE>_URL). The `graph-driver-optional` invariant is the
one case that runs WITHOUT a live engine (it asserts the missing-driver error
and that the core imports driver-free).
STATUS: OWED in all four - greenfield. No framework ships a graph layer yet, so
every invariant carries `cases: []` with the real case names parked in
`proposed_cases` and the intended per-language suite files in `proposed_suites`.
scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py therefore reports these as OWED (declared,
not yet proven) rather than FAIL. Contract authored BEFORE any code, per
PORTING-FORMULA.md (audit -> neutral contract -> all implementations).
Build order (ADR-0059): the standalone tina4stack/ultipa-<lang> drivers first,
then per framework the graph/ module (mirroring database/) with adapters
ultipa / bolt [Neo4j+Memgraph] / arango. Flip owed -> proven per
framework+engine only when the named suite carries the case against that engine.

invariants.rule: GraphDatabase.create(url) selects the adapter from the URL scheme (ultipa:// -> Ultipa, neo4j://|bolt:// -> Bolt/Neo4j, memgraph:// -> Bolt/Memgraph, arango://|arangodb:// -> Arango) and returns a connected adapter. fromEnv() does the same from TINA4_GRAPH_URL.
invariants.why: URL-driven selection is the whole point of the Database-shaped design: one factory, engine chosen by scheme, no per-engine construction code in the app.
proposed_cases: a URL scheme selects the right adapter and connects

invariants.rule: addNode(label, properties) creates a vertex and returns a GraphNode { id, labels, properties } with a non-null id and the stored properties echoed back.
invariants.why: The portable node create is the base of the unified surface; the returned id is what every edge and read depends on.
proposed_cases: addNode returns a node with an id, labels and properties

invariants.rule: addEdge(fromId, toId, type, properties) links two existing nodes and returns a GraphEdge { id, type, from, to, properties } with from/to matching the arguments.
invariants.why: Edges are the reason a graph engine exists; the from/to/type contract must mean the same thing on every engine.
proposed_cases: addEdge links two nodes with a type and properties

invariants.rule: getNode(id) returns the stored GraphNode with its properties intact (round-trip), and returns a null/None/nil for an id that does not exist (a miss is not an error).
invariants.why: Read-back parity proves the write persisted and the neutral node shape survives the engine's own storage/types.
proposed_cases: getNode of a missing id returns a falsy value, not an error

invariants.rule: updateNode(id, properties) merges the properties (verified by re-read); deleteNode(id) removes the node so a subsequent getNode(id) is a miss.
invariants.why: Mutation + removal complete the portable node lifecycle and prove the changes are durable, not client-side.
proposed_cases: updateNode merges properties, verified by re-read
deleteNode removes the node, verified by re-read

invariants.rule: neighbors(id, { direction, edgeType, limit }) returns the directly-connected nodes filtered by direction (out/in/both) and optional edge type; an unmatched filter returns empty, not an error.
invariants.why: One-hop traversal is the most common graph read; direction and edge-type filtering must be uniform across engines.
proposed_cases: neighbors returns the connected nodes for a direction and edge type

invariants.rule: traverse(startId, { depth }) returns the set of nodes reachable within `depth` hops from the start (the start's own inclusion is defined and consistent across engines).
invariants.why: Bounded multi-hop traversal is the portable stand-in for each engine's native path query; the reachable set must agree on all engines for the same graph.
proposed_cases: traverse to depth N returns the reachable set

invariants.rule: query(text, params) runs the engine's NATIVE read language (GQL/UQL on Ultipa, Cypher on Neo4j/Memgraph, AQL on ArangoDB) with bound params and returns a GraphResult (records + columns), same shape as the relational DatabaseResult. execute(text, params) does the same for a write.
invariants.why: The raw pass-through is the escape hatch that keeps the portable core small; it must bind params (no string interpolation) and return the uniform result shape.
proposed_cases: a native-dialect query round-trips through query() with bound params

invariants.rule: A malformed or failing raw statement RAISES (never a falsy return); the cause is readable via getError() after the raise. Mirrors the relational execute()/fetch() fail-loud contract.
invariants.why: A swallowed graph write is the same silent-data-loss footgun the SQL layer already outlawed; the negative proves errors surface.
proposed_cases: a bad raw statement raises and records the cause on getError()

invariants.rule: The graph core imports and runs with NO engine driver installed. Opening a connection whose engine driver is absent raises an actionable error naming the missing package and the install command. (Runs without a live engine.)
invariants.why: The zero-dependency-core rule is load-bearing: a graph driver must be a cost paid only when the engine is used, exactly like the SQL drivers.
proposed_cases: a missing engine driver raises an actionable install error
the graph core imports with no graph driver present

invariants.rule: A connect to an unreachable host throws within TINA4_GRAPH_CONNECT_TIMEOUT seconds, naming the host, port and elapsed seconds (mirrors the relational TINA4_DATABASE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT contract).
invariants.why: An unbounded graph connect hangs the app with no signal, the exact failure the relational connect-timeout contract exists to prevent; the graph layer must inherit it.
proposed_cases: an unreachable host times out within the configured bound, naming host and port
